title: Nancy Mace discusses government funding vote and local nonprofit engagement - Berkeley Leader
text:
Rep. Nancy Mace, a U.S. Congresswoman representing South Carolina’s 1st district since 2021, posted several updates on her official Twitter account on February 4, 2026, addressing family priorities, government funding for the military, and local nonprofit engagement.
In a tweet published at 2:37 a.m., Mace posed a question to her followers: “If you could do one thing for your family tomorrow, what would it be?” (February 4, 2026).
Later that morning at 3:15 a.m., she commented on recent legislative action regarding government operations and military compensation. She wrote: “We voted YES to reopen the government and to give our troops their pay, their benefits, and the resources they need to do their jobs effectively and safely. Our men and women in uniform shouldn’t miss a single paycheck while defending this nation. We will always stand on the https://t.co/3tApktxboQ” (February 4, 2026).
By midday at 12:45 p.m., Mace reported her office’s participation in a community event focused on nonprofit organizations in Summerville. She stated: “Our office attended the Summerville Chamber Nonprofit Council, to both addresses and learn about issues and concerns affecting nonprofit organizations. This gave us the opportunity to see where our congressional support is needed and allows us to connects with various https://t.co/YDEpP3Bfon” (February 4, 2026).
Mace has represented South Carolina’s coastal district since succeeding Joe Cunningham in Congress in January 2021. Before serving in Congress, she was elected to the South Carolina House of Representatives from 2018 through 2020. Born in Fort Bragg in 1977 and now residing in Charleston, Mace graduated from The Citadel with a Bachelor of Science degree in 1999.
